Russia.

So, Aunt May’s knitting club decided to take their "stitch and bitch" session to a whole new level of chaos. The plan was simple: knit, chat, and ignore the fact that their feline overlord, Mr. Whiskers, had just discovered the joy of unraveling.

It started innocently enough. One minute, Mrs. Higgins was complaining about her grandson’s lack of ambition, and the next, a loud *thwump* echoed from the corner. There sat Mr. Whiskers, batting at a loose end of yarn with the precision of a bomb disposal expert. By the time Aunt May noticed, it was too late. The cat had decided that the intricate cable-knit sweater she’d been working on for three weeks was not a garment, but a puzzle to be solved.

What followed was a trail of woolly breadcrumbs that would have made Hansel and Gretel jealous. It wasn’t just a mess; it was a labyrinth. You couldn’t walk to the kitchen without stepping on a loop of wool. You couldn’t sit on the couch without sinking into a nest of unraveling cashmere. At one point, Mrs. Higgins tried to shoo the cat away, but she only succeeded in tangling her own cardigan in the disaster zone.

The real kicker? Mr. Whiskers looked at the pile of yarn, looked at the horrified women, and then deliberately sat on the largest ball of it, purring loudly as if to say, "I didn’t do it. I was just... organizing."

Aunt May’s knitting club disbanded that day. Not because they ran out of yarn, but because they realized they were competing with a cat who had no respect for deadlines, patterns, or personal space. And honestly? I think Mr. Whiskers won.
